research_page.title: Disease-Associated Microglia (DAM) and TREM2 in AD (Cell, 2017)
research_page.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals a unique, TREM2-dependent microglia state (DAM) that colocalizes with Aβ plaques.
research_page.takeaway_md: This foundational preclinical study identified "Disease-Associated Microglia" (DAM), a specialized cellular state that clusters around amyloid plaques and phagocytoses them. It demonstrated that transitioning to this protective state requires the TREM2 receptor, a finding that sparked massive biopharma investment in TREM2-activating drugs.
key_findings_md: Researchers identified a novel subset of microglia, termed DAM, by mapping immune populations in wild-type and Alzheimer's transgenic mouse brains.
DAMs colocalize with amyloid plaques and contain intracellular Aβ particles, suggesting a phagocytic role.
The activation of the DAM program is a two-step process: an initial Trem2-independent downregulation of microglial checkpoints, followed by Trem2-dependent full activation.
research_page.methods_md: Single-cell RNA sequencing and immunohistochemical analysis of wild-type mice, Alzheimer's transgenic (Tg-AD) mice, Trem2-knockout (Trem2−/−) Tg-AD mice, and human brain slices.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: While this paper positioned TREM2-dependent DAMs as a highly promising therapeutic target to restrict neurodegeneration, clinical translation has proven difficult. The first major test of this hypothesis in humans, the TREM2 agonistic antibody [AL002](/trials/al002-invoke-2-nct04592874), failed to slow cognitive decline in a Phase 2 trial and increased amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).
research_page.sentiment_md: Perception of this hypothesis is sharply divided. The scientific and investment communities (e.g., driving Sanofi's acquisition of Vigil Neuroscience) enthusiastically embraced TREM2 agonists as a potential paradigm shift. However, commercial discourse frequently oversimplifies DAMs as universally protective, overlooking emerging scientific nuance that these microglia can become senescent or harmful over time.
caveats_md: The mechanistic description of the two-step DAM activation relies almost exclusively on transgenic mouse models, which may not accurately reflect human Alzheimer's pathophysiology.
Subsequent clinical failures of TREM2 agonists strongly suggest that pharmacologically forcing this microglial state in humans does not safely or effectively restrict neurodegeneration.
relates_to_md: [AL002 Phase 2 (INVOKE-2)](/trials/al002-invoke-2-nct04592874) — The leading clinical test of the TREM2 agonist hypothesis, which failed.
[Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — DAMs act primarily by phagocytosing amyloid-beta plaques.

trial_pages.title: INVOKE-2: AL002 Phase 2 in Early AD
trial_pages.description: Phase 2 trial evaluating the TREM2 agonistic antibody AL002 in early Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.why_md: This trial was the first major clinical test of the hypothesis that pharmacological TREM2 activation can stimulate disease-associated microglia (DAM) to clear amyloid plaques and slow progression. Its failure raises significant questions about the viability of targeting TREM2 in human patients.
status_log_md: **2024-08** — Trial reads out, missing its primary clinical endpoint.
trial_pages.results_md: The trial failed to meet its primary and secondary endpoints; AL002 did not significantly change the CDR-SB score versus placebo. Additionally, the drug induced amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), leading to the termination of its open-label extension.

timeline_entries.title: 2017-06 — Discovery of Disease-Associated Microglia (DAM)
timeline_entries.body_md: Researchers map a novel, TREM2-dependent microglial state that clusters around amyloid plaques, sparking a wave of biotech investment into TREM2 agonists. Detailed in [Keren-Shaul et al.](/research/papers/disease-associated-microglia-cell-2017).

timeline_entries.title: 2024-08 — First TREM2 agonist fails in Phase 2
timeline_entries.body_md: The leading TREM2-activating antibody, [AL002](/trials/al002-invoke-2-nct04592874), fails to slow cognitive decline and induces ARIA in the INVOKE-2 trial, casting doubt on the microglial activation hypothesis.
